boardNames: American Board of Pathology (ABPath) primary certification: Anatomic Pathology (AP), Clinical Pathology (CP), combined AP/CP; AP/Neuropathology (AP/NP) where eligible; each has distinct prerequisites and exams.
ABPath subspecialty examinations: Blood Banking/Transfusion Medicine; Cytopathology; Dermatopathology (in cooperation with ABD); Hematopathology; Medical Microbiology; Neuropathology.
No separate ABPath subspecialty examination is listed for breast pathology or gastrointestinal pathology; these BIDMC offerings should not be represented as a separate ABPath board credential.
boardStatus: No single board exam for the directory category. ABPath offers primary AP/CP and separate subspecialty exams in some listed fields. ABPath’s published subspecialty list does not separately list breast or GI pathology; do not infer a standalone board credential from the institution’s fellowship names. This is a date-checked catalogue distinction, not an eligibility determination.
boardEligibilityNotice: Eligibility is controlled by the relevant board and program, including prerequisites, accredited training, and current rules. This independent course does not create board eligibility or certification. Verify directly with ABPath and any cooperating board (e.g., ABD for dermatopathology).

level: Clinical physician residency; institutional AP-only, CP-only, combined AP/CP, and AP/NP variants are preserved explicitly. This independent course is a combined AP/CP-oriented self-study spine, with NP and subspecialty material labeled as extension.-aligned independent study

studyHours.plan: Suggested independent-study plan, not observed time and not residency time: the complete duration-observed public video sequence (see verifiedExternalHours) plus 140h readings and notes, 110h case/slide practice on linked source sites, 30h original-question/rationale review, and 20h portfolio and revision. The lecture total is the sum of exact unique durations, not estimated study time. Do not add these study-plan hours to verified video hours. No rotations, supervision, procedures, case logs or service work are included.

boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course does not grant board eligibility, accredited training, licensure, procedural competence, or certification. Confirm the current Board booklet and ACGME requirements directly. No pass guarantee.

boardStatus: A distinct physician clinical subspecialty with a jointly developed Adolescent Medicine certification examination program (ABP, ABIM, ABFM); the ABP states it administers the exam. ABFM uses a CAQ pathway and states continuing-certification candidates transition to longitudinal assessment. Board titles/pathways and maintenance differ. This is not a generic directory category or research-only/non-physician track. The fellowship is not a combined Med-Peds residency; prior internal medicine/pediatrics residency can be an entry route. Hopkins page separately notes optional addiction medicine training and a possible separate Addiction Medicine board exam.
boardEligibilityNotice: This course does not establish eligibility. ABP route requires primary board certification accepted by ABP, three years full-time broad-based ACGME/RCPSC-accredited adolescent-medicine fellowship training, program-director evaluation/scholarly requirements and passing the exam. ABIM’s current policy lists primary ABIM certification, 24 months fellowship including 12 clinical months, licensure/competence and passing its pathway exam. ABFM requires its separate application/eligibility review for CAQ. Confirm current policies with the board for the candidate’s primary certification and jurisdiction.

boardStatus.status: The ABP publishes a General Pediatrics initial certifying examination and a corresponding public content outline, which also applies to ITE, MOC and MOCA-Peds assessments. This is a physician board certification pathway, distinct from ACGME programme accreditation and local BCRP curriculum.
boardStatus.separateBoardExam: Yes: ABP General Pediatrics initial certifying examination exists. No separate ABP board exam is associated merely with the Categorical or LEAD BCRP tracks. BCRP combined programmes have additional discipline-specific certification pathways; their exact requirements are set by each other certifying board and are outside this general-pediatrics curriculum.
boardStatus.blueprintScope: ABP 2024 General Pediatrics Content Outline (effective for exams from Oct 15, 2024; minor revisions Dec 2024): 24 domains weighted from Preventive Pediatrics/Well-Child Care (12%) to Genetics/Dysmorphology/Metabolic Disorders (2%), Rheumatology (2%), Ethics (2%), and Patient Safety/Quality Improvement/Research Methods (2%). Four universal tasks: physiology/pathophysiology; epidemiology/risk assessment; diagnosis; management/treatment. See official outline; mappings in this course are study aids, not exam predictions.
boardStatus.eligibilitySummary: ABP admission requires an eligible medical-school degree, satisfactory completion of full accredited pediatric residency (three years for ACGME; four years for RCPSC under rules effective Jan 2025), qualifying unrestricted U.S./Canada license, and programme-director verification; consult ABP for current rule text and individual determination.

boardEligibilityNotice: This independent self-study course confers no medical degree, ACGME/RCPSC training credit, supervised clinical experience or case volume, ABP or other board eligibility, license, clinical competence, credential, accreditation, or likelihood of passing. ABP and other boards determine eligibility under their current rules. It grants no institutional affiliation, and it cannot replace accredited residency or supervised care.

boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course does not create board eligibility. The ABP says a Pediatrics-Anesthesiology applicant must complete joint training in an integrated ACGME-accredited program and may not take the ABP certifying exam until all training in both programs is complete. The ABA separately administers BASIC, ADVANCED and APPLIED examination components. Confirm current requirements directly with ABP, ABA, ACGME and the program.

boardNames: American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — General Pediatrics certification examination only; no separate Academic General Pediatrics board examination
boardStatus: Academic General Pediatrics has no separate board certification. APA lists an academic general pediatrics fellowship accreditation category; that is distinct from ACGME program accreditation and ABP certification. boardEligibilityNotice: This course confers no eligibility. Refer to ABP General Pediatrics admission requirements and the candidate’s own accredited residency/board status; fellowship participation or course completion does not establish eligibility. No passing outcome is promised.
